items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled theorem at source lines 1080-1093 (book Theorem 8.4.6): a pointed map f : X \to Y with fiber F gives a long exact sequence of homotopy groups, which are groups except in the last three terms and abelian except in the last six. The statement records only the sequence and the algebraic structure, while the proof (source lines 1100-1129) has to establish exactness at every term: it reduces the theorem to exactness of the 0-truncation of a fiber sequence, proves the inclusion im \subseteq ker from functoriality together with f \circ g = 0, and then has to show ker \subseteq im for an element given only as a truncated equality, which forces two successive truncation inductions: one to lift the element of the 0-truncation to an element w of W, and one that uses the path-truncation equivalence to turn \tproj0{f(w)} = \tproj0{z_0} into a genuine path p : f(w) = z_0, after which (w,p) is the required preimage. The identification of the later maps with the negative of the induced maps on homotopy groups, and the resulting group and abelian-group structure, are then read off with thm:fiber-of-the-fiber and the Eckmann-Hilton argument; nothing of this reduction is visible in the statement.
